<thought>From the ESI mass spectrum, the most intense ion is at m/z 114.06808, which corresponds to the protonated molecule [M+H]+. Subtracting the mass of a proton (1.007276 Da) gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈113.0608 Da. The formula C₆H₉O₂ has a calculated monoisotopic mass of 113.0603 Da, matching the observed mass within a few ppm. The relative intensity of the M+1 peak (~6.7 %) is consistent with the natural 13C abundance for six carbons, supporting this formula. Therefore the molecular formula of the sample compound is C6H9O2.</thought>
<final_answer>C6H9O2</final_answer>
